question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z<1.68).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9515\,$ | $\,0.9525\,$ | $\,0.9535\,$ |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9608\,$ | $\,0.9616\,$ | $\,0.9625\,$ |
| $\,1.8\,$ | $\,0.9686\,$ | $\,0.9693\,$ | $\,0.9699\,$ |

$P(Z<1.68)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
If $Z∼N(0,1),$ then by the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Also, since $Z$ is continuous, 

$$
P(Z<1.68)=P(Z\le 1.68)=Φ(1.68).
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/244c5a3af574c72e499c5e2dd14c81e3d202b903300344b85e42e4bf5129f0c7.png)

Now, we determine the value of $Φ(1.68)$ from the table:

- We first select the row that corresponds to $1.6$ and the column that corresponds to $0.08.$

- Then, we take the value that lies at the intersection:

| $z$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9515\,$ | $\,0.9525\,$ | $\,0.9535\,$ |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9608\,$ | $\,0.9616\,$ | $\,0.9625\,$ |
| $\,1.8\,$ | $\,0.9686\,$ | $\,0.9693\,$ | $\,0.9699\,$ |

Therefore, according to the table, we have

$$
P(Z\le 1.68)=Φ(1.68)=0.9535.
$$
